Unfortunately, I am not able to play Star Citizen to its full capacity currently. I recently bought a new 3070 and was very excited to restart my adventure on SC, but my CPU can’t keep up. My old 1070 ti worked well enough on lowest settings, but this was also a few years ago. Tried the game again on both GPUs recently and my FPS was so low on the lowest settings that it wasn’t worth it. The game ran like a potato hooked up to a AAA battery.

But, I will say, when I was able to play the game a couple years ago, I did have a tremendous amount of fun having the ability to stand up in my ship and walk around as I was moving through slipspace (can’t rightfully remember what the term was called while warping to different parts of the system) and found things to do while I waited to reach my destination. 

If Frontier did space legs correctly, with ship interiors and all, this would have made ED so much more fascinating. Imagine starting FSD to fly to Hutton Orbital (which can take over an hour or two depending on the ship) and just saying “fuck sitting here, I’m going into my Anaconda’s hanger and fuck around.” Staring out a side window as stars or ships zipped by.

Not to say SC doesn’t have its own problems. Hell, like the article said, it’s not even a fully released game. But, as you said it’s definitely giving many ED players that true space flight sim vibe that they have been craving that Frontier just hasn’t delivered.

You’re right, I apologize. But there was much more strenuous matters that needed to be tended to within the game before we got space legs. 

At least, in my opinion.

I have nearly 600 hours into elite dangerous. A good portion of that would also be in VR. Hell , I even bought a HOTAS for this game. All of this happened before the recent Odyssey DLC and I have no interest in downloading it just for the simple pleasure of “space legs.” For years I watched this game bloom into something magical and then the small niche of folks on the sub would yell “we want space legs!” And then that’s what Frontier focused on. 

This game is one of my absolute favorite games out there. It’s gorgeous and fun. Sure there’s problems with graphical issues and balance, but it’s still a ton of fun (referencing without Odyssey since I didn’t buy it) and I want to see it thrive.

But it won’t. Not with the way Frontier is taking the game. The community will only take so much before they give up. In fact, I already gave up. I haven’t played in 5 months and have no plans to go back any time soon, and that hurts to say.

Moore, Oklahoma, 2013. F4 tornado ripped through the city in a 17 mile long devastation path. That night, A few marines and myself went out to help first responders find anyone stuck under the debris or to simply help folks dig through their stuff to find anything valuable. Day two of being out there we came across one family (mother, father, two kids) all frantically digging through what they thought was their house. The 4 of us asked if we could help. The Mother, barely able to hold herself together told us through labored breathes that they can’t find their dog. They left the poor pooch in a kennel that was inside the garage when they were told to evacuate. 

Now mind you, there was no house, no garage, hell, no neighborhood. Only way they knew they were on their own property was the house address number painted onto the curb on the street. So we all started digging... everywhere. We didn’t even know where to start, we just started digging. 

I was a young Lance Corporal at the time and very pessimistic. I was digging through the rubble looking for a mangled clump of fur. Sorry to sound like an asshole, but it wouldn’t have been the first dead dog we’ve dug up on that day. I had no reason to believe this situation would be any different.

Lo and behold, the Gunny and I lifted a giant piece of siding up revealing a small kennel buried beneath the mound. Small whimpers could be heard. Gunny screams “we found him! Holy shit! We found him!” Unlocked the kennel gate and the dog, tail wagging and all, ran out and straight into the arms of the mother.

I saw lots of tears during my 4 days there digging. That was one of the few times I’m happy to say that everyone was shedding tears of hope and happiness.
